question: Does the cited 1993 NPC-reservoir fisheries chapter or accessible secondary literature provide Caliraya- or Lumot-specific historical fish records that can be safely distinguished from grouped stocking context?

scope.notes: The FAO review calls the combined system Caliraya-Lumot when discussing reservoir catch or limnological information. Its separate stocking table names Caliraya among a four-reservoir group but does not name Lumot.

sourcesReviewed.title: Social, Economic and Cultural Aspects in Implementing Inland Fishery Enhancements in the Philippines
sourcesReviewed.citation: dela Cruz, C.R. 1998. In T. Petr (ed.), Inland fishery enhancements. FAO Fisheries Technical Paper No. 374. Rome: FAO. The official volume page identifies the work as a 463-page 1998 publication; chapter pagination was not verified.
findings: The chapter says its review is based on literature, including unpublished reports, and discussions with researchers and administrators; it is not itself a primary Caliraya-Lumot survey.
It names Caliraya-Lumot among seven hydroelectric reservoir systems for which catch data and/or limnological information were available, citing Balite (1993) and other reservoir studies.
Its annual catch table lists Ambuklao, Angat, Binga, Magat, Pantabangan, and Pulangui IV; it supplies no Caliraya- or Lumot-specific catch series in that table.

A historical stocking table is headed for Ambuklao, Angat, Binga, and Caliraya reservoirs collectively. It does not allocate each listed species to an individual reservoir, and the heading does not include Lumot.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official FAO chapter and volume title page reviewed online. No local copy retained.

sourcesReviewed.title: Status of Fish Production and Management of Fisheries in the Reservoirs of NPC Hydroelectric Power Plants (HEPs)
sourcesReviewed.citation: Balite, L.R. 1993. Chapter in R.C. Sevilleja, E.V. Manalili, and R.D. Guerrero III (eds.), Reservoir Fisheries Management and Development in the Philippines, PCAMRD Book Series No. 17/1993. The original chapter was not retrieved; its page range remains unresolved.
sourcesReviewed.access: Bibliographic citation leads were reviewed, but no copy of the proceedings or chapter text was located. An AGRIS record for a different chapter in the same proceedings provides volume-level metadata only.

sourcesReviewed.title: Commercially Caught Freshwater Fishes in the Philippines: Status, Issues, and Recommendations
sourcesReviewed.citation: Guerrero, R.D. 2022. Transactions of the National Academy of Science and Technology Philippines 44. DOI: 10.57043/transnastphl.2022.2568.
sourcesReviewed.sourceType: National inland-fisheries review; used here only as a citation cross-check
sourcesReviewed.finding: Its bibliography cites the Balite chapter as pages 11-20, differing from the FAO chapter's pages 21-52. It does not provide the underlying 1993 chapter or resolve this discrepancy.
sourcesReviewed.license: CC BY 4.0 for the 2022 NAST article; this license does not establish reuse rights for the separately cited 1993 proceedings chapter.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official NAST-hosted article PDF reviewed online.

retrieval.target: Original Balite (1993) proceedings chapter and any Caliraya-Lumot-specific tables or monitoring records
searches: Exact-title and book-series searches across indexed FAO AGRIS/official-source results did not locate the Balite chapter text.

A University of the Philippines at Los Baños-provided AGRIS record for another contribution confirms the proceedings title, editors, publisher, ISBN 971-8624-19-8, and conference date, but is not the Balite chapter and contains no Balite data.

limits: The FAO review is historical and literature-based; it does not establish present-day occurrence, abundance, catchability, or a complete fish checklist.
Grouped stocking cohorts cannot be assigned to Caliraya individually, and they provide no Lumot-specific species attribution.
The catch table omits Caliraya-Lumot and cannot be used to infer zero catch or fish absence there.
The 1993 Balite chapter is still unretrieved; its page-range conflict is unresolved until the original proceedings are checked.
The FAO volume page displays a 1998 copyright notice; no item-specific open license or public-app reuse permission was verified.
nextAction: Try an authorized library or agency catalog route for the original proceedings, asking first whether the Balite chapter or relevant reservoir tables are available. In parallel, continue with a distinct CALABARZON freshwater source that exposes a complete, dated, waterbody-resolved fish table and item-level reuse terms.
